summary: VectorLift peak autoscaler oscillation causing long-tail 5xx, streaming truncation, and SLA breach (post-incident action plan)
description:
Issue summary:
During VectorLift's weekday peak (2026-03-10 00:45-02:15 UTC) we observed autoscaler oscillation on their Dedicated GPU pool in us-east which led to cascading long-tail 5xx errors and truncated streaming sessions for long chat conversations. Impact: customer-facing timeouts and truncated transcripts across ~18% of in-flight requests, increased retry amplification leading to a billing delta, and an SLA breach for VectorLift's enterprise contract.

Impact:
- ~18% of streams returned 5xx or were truncated mid-stream for sessions longer than 8k tokens.
- Elevated tail latency (p95->p99) from 420ms to 5.8s for affected model routes.
- Autoscaler thrash caused short-lived GPU pool evictions; multiple requests re-routed to fallback variants which increased token consumption.
- Customer experienced elevated error rates and reported percent of customer-facing production calls failed, prompting an urgent escalation.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 00:40 UTC: VectorLift reports elevated streaming truncations via #support channel.
- 2026-03-10 00:45 UTC: Support triage, linked incident INC-2026-0310-VL-OSC created.
- 2026-03-10 00:50 UTC: SRE observes autoscaler cycling events in us-east dedicated pool.
- 2026-03-10 01:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: increase autoscaler min replicas and pinned pool to conservative scaling thresholds.
- 2026-03-10 01:20 UTC: Error rate begins to subside; streaming truncation reports drop to <2%.
- 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC: Post-incident review call with VectorLift; action items assigned.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Send sustained high-concurrency long-session (8k+ token) streaming load against VectorLift's dedicated endpoint (us-east) using redwood/realtime-chat-rlhf-7b routed to autoscaled pool.
2. Observe autoscaler CPU/KV eviction metrics; watch for scale-down events occurring within <90s of scale-up under the current policy.
3. Confirm fallback routing to quantized variants and increased retry amplification.

Logs and signals:
- Dashboards: link to SRE dashboard (internal) and VectorLift per-route telemetry.
- Kashti traces show inflight queue length spike peaking at 3.2k concurrent requests.
- Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up then immediate scale-down decisions driven by short-duration concurrency bursts.
- Serving runtime logs indicate increased KV prefix evictions and occasional OOM warnings on a subset of models.

Current status:
- Root cause identified as aggressive autoscaler cooldown and threshold settings combined with workload shape (short, high-concurrency bursts of long-session streams).
- Temporary mitigations remain in place for VectorLift; engineering rollback to conservative autoscaler config performed and verified in us-east.
- Billing adjustment negotiated and credited (see billing_adjustment).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Autoscaler cooldown/threshold misconfiguration caused oscillation when encountering short spikes; evidence: scale events logged every 60-110s during incident window.
Hypothesis B: Workload shape (many long-session streams with similar start times) amplified inflight queue leading to KV cache churn and transient OOMs on quantized kernels.
Finding: p95 token latency correlated strongly with autoscaler downscale events (Pearson r=0.78), and OOMs aligned with peak inflight queue times.
Observed: Fallback routing to gptx-13b-q4-hotfix variants increased token counts per request by ~12% due to expanded decoding artifacts, contributing to billing delta.
Logs: SRE pulled logs from serving-runtime (2026-03-10T00:44 - 2026-03-10T01:30) and autoscaler controller; artifacts uploaded to internal storage.
resolution: Applied temporary fix by raising autoscaler minimum replicas for VectorLift's pool and increasing scale-down cooldown to 600s. Rolled back recent aggressive scaling policy from rollout v3.2.1 to v3.1.8 for the affected customer pool. Verified streaming success rates returned to baseline within 35 minutes. Scheduled durable fixes: implement workload-aware scaling policy that factors in session length and token-budget, add per-customer canary window for aggressive autoscaler rollouts, and add alarms for repeated up/down cycles. Engineering PRs prepared (see related_github_prs).
billing_adjustment: Applied one-time credit covering estimated token amplification and retry costs for the incident window: $14,250 credited to VectorLift's account. Finance notified and invoice adjusted.
